## Overview

Taxonomic revisions and descriptions of new species cite the specimens examined for each species, in a format that differs from journal to journal: the header, the case and format (bold, italics, small capitals) of countries, states and collectors, how dates and coordinates are written, and how herbaria are listed.

The function `barroso_write_specimens()` writes these lists for one, several or all species of a database of herbarium records into a Word (.docx) file, in the format of a chosen journal. This article goes through the whole workflow with two R scripts, using the herbarium records of *Luetzelburgia* (Leguminosae), a genus of 15 species of South American trees:

1. `01_get_standardized_records_script.R` downloads the records from GBIF, REFLORA and JABOT, combines and standardizes them, and saves a spreadsheet;
2. `02_write_examined_specimens_script.R` writes the lists of examined specimens from this spreadsheet, in the format of several journals.

Both scripts are run from an RStudio project, e.g. `build_herbarium_records_database`, with the scripts in a folder `scripts` and the results saved in a folder `results`.

## Script 1: get standardized records

The records are downloaded with [plantR](https://github.com/LimaRAF/plantR) (GBIF), [refloraR](https://dboslab.github.io/refloraR-website/) (REFLORA Virtual Herbarium) and [jabotR](https://dboslab.github.io/jabotR-website/) (JABOT, Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden). The list of accepted species comes from Kew's [WCVP](https://powo.science.kew.org/), with the package `rWCVPdata`.

```r
# 01_get_standardized_records_script.R

library(barRoso)
library(refloraR)
library(jabotR)
library(plantR)
library(dplyr)
library(openxlsx)
library(rWCVPdata)

# Create a folder for the results of today
dir <- "results"
folder_name <- paste0(dir, "/", format(Sys.time(), "%d%b%Y"))
if (!dir.exists(folder_name)) dir.create(folder_name, recursive = TRUE)

# All accepted species of Luetzelburgia in WCVP
wcvp_names <- rWCVPdata::wcvp_names
luetz_wcvp <- subset(wcvp_names,
                     genus == "Luetzelburgia" &
                       taxon_rank == "Species" &
                       taxon_status == "Accepted")
luetz_list <- sort(luetz_wcvp$taxon_name)

# GBIF: one search for each species, skipping species without records
data_gbif <- lapply(luetz_list, function(x) {
  gbif <- tryCatch(plantR::rgbif2(species = x, n.records = 5000, force = TRUE,
                                  remove_na = FALSE, save = FALSE, compress = FALSE),
                   error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.data.frame(gbif) || nrow(gbif) == 0) return(NULL)
  gbif
})
names(data_gbif) <- luetz_list
data_gbif <- dplyr::bind_rows(data_gbif, .id = "original_search")

# REFLORA Virtual Herbarium
data_reflora <- refloraR::reflora_records(repatriated = TRUE, taxon = "Luetzelburgia",
                                          indets = TRUE, updates = TRUE,
                                          verbose = TRUE, save = FALSE)
unlink("reflora_download/", recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)

# JABOT
data_jabot <- jabotR::jabot_records(taxon = "Luetzelburgia", indets = TRUE,
                                    updates = TRUE, verbose = TRUE, save = FALSE)
unlink("jabot_download/", recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)

# Combine the sources, keeping GBIF for the herbaria present in more than one
records_list <- list(GBIF = data_gbif,
                     REFLORA = data_reflora,
                     JABOT = data_jabot)
data_all <- barRoso::barroso_cat(list_sources = records_list,
                                 keep_source = "GBIF")

# Standardize collectors, herbaria, places and taxa, and remove duplicates
data_all_clean <- barRoso::barroso_std(data_all,
                                       unvouchered = TRUE,
                                       delunkcoll = TRUE,
                                       flag_duplicates = TRUE,
                                       rm_duplicates = TRUE)

# Fix and flag coordinates
data_all_clean <- barRoso::std_coordinates(data_all_clean)

# Save the database
openxlsx::write.xlsx(data_all_clean,
                     paste0(folder_name, "/Luetzelburgia_herbarium_records.xlsx"))
```

In November 2026, this script found 3,215 records in GBIF, 1,093 in REFLORA and 351 in JABOT:

```
#> barroso_cat: removing 1089 records of 39 herbaria from REFLORA also present in GBIF
#> barroso_cat: removing 337 records of 10 herbaria from JABOT also present in GBIF
```

After the standardization, without duplicates, unvouchered records and records of unknown collectors, the database has 1,202 records of 15 species, from Brazil (1,155), Bolivia (35), Colombia (3) and Guyana (3).

## Script 2: write the examined specimens

The second script reads the spreadsheet saved by the first one, and writes one .docx file for each journal, in the same folder:

```r
# 02_write_examined_specimens_script.R

library(barRoso)
library(openxlsx)

# The most recent spreadsheet within the results folder
dir <- "results"
records_files <- list.files(dir,
                            pattern = "^Luetzelburgia_herbarium_records[.]xlsx$",
                            recursive = TRUE,
                            full.names = TRUE)
records_file <- records_files[which.max(file.mtime(records_files))]
folder_name <- dirname(records_file)

# Read the records once, so the spreadsheet is not read again for each journal
data_records <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(records_file)

# One Word (.docx) file for each journal. To write just some species, use the
# argument species, e.g. species = c("Luetzelburgia andina", "Luetzelburgia harleyi")
journals <- c("Annals of the Missouri Botanical Garden",
              "Systematic Botany",
              "Kew Bulletin",
              "Rodriguesia")

for (journal in journals) {
  barRoso::barroso_write_specimens(
    df = data_records,
    species = NULL,
    journal = journal,
    dir = folder_name,
    filename = paste0("Luetzelburgia_examined_specimens_", gsub("\\s+", "_", journal))
  )
}
#> Skipping 5 records not identified to species
#> Examined specimens of 15 species (1131 specimens) written in the format of
#> Annals of the Missouri Botanical Garden to:
#> results/01Nov2026/Luetzelburgia_examined_specimens_Annals_of_the_Missouri_Botanical_Garden.docx
#> ...
```

For each species, the file has the species name and its author, followed by a paragraph with its specimens, e.g. in the format of Systematic Botany:

> ***Luetzelburgia auriculata*** **(Allemão) Ducke**
>
> ***Representative Specimens Examined***—**Brazil.** —<span style="font-variant: small-caps;">Bahia</span>: Barreiras, Prainha, margem do Rio das Ondas, 12°08′48″S, 45°00′55″W, 1 May 2009, *D. Cardoso 2628* (HUEFS). —<span style="font-variant: small-caps;">Ceará</span>: Caucaia, Lagoa dos Caetanos, 3°S, 38°W, 21 Jan 2009, *D. Cardoso et al. 2379* (ASE, BOTU, CNMT, HDJF, HEPH, HUCS, HUEFS, HUESB, SORO, UB, UESC, VIC); Crateús, RPPN Serra das Almas, 5°09′44″S, 40°53′18″W, 15 Jun 2014, *F.H.F. Nascimento 1402* (HUEFS).

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `df` or `path` | The records, as a data frame or an .xlsx/.csv file, in Darwin Core format (e.g. the output of `barroso_std()` or `barroso_dwc()`) |
| `species` | Species to write, with or without authors (e.g. `"Luetzelburgia andina"`); `NULL` for all species |
| `journal` | The journal whose format is followed, one of the 24 journals below |
| `header` | Text of the header, e.g. `"Paratypes"` or `"Additional specimens examined"`; `NULL` for the header of the journal, `""` for no header |
| `language` | Language of the paper: `"en"` (English), `"pt"` (Portuguese) or `"es"` (Spanish), for the header (e.g. `"Material examinado"`), months, countries (`"BRASIL"`), phenology (`"fl. e fr."`, `"est."`) and the west hemisphere in Spanish (`"O"`) |
| `catalog_numbers` | If `TRUE`, the catalog number is written after each herbarium, e.g. `"IAC no. 14754"` in Brittonia |
| `dir`, `filename` | Folder and name of the .docx file |
| `font_family`, `font_size` | Font of the document |

## Journal formats

The `journal` argument lists all available formats, each checked against recent papers of the journal, including the bold, italics and small capitals used. The journal can be written in any case, with or without accents, and abbreviated, e.g. `"systematic botany"`, `"Kew"`, `"Edinburgh"` or `"Rodriguesia"`. The examples below show the same records of *Luetzelburgia auriculata* in each format, as written in the .docx file. The records of *D. Cardoso et al. 2379* and *D. Machado Cardoso 2379* are duplicates of the same collection, and are cited once, with all their herbaria.

## How the specimens are written

- **Columns.** The function uses the Darwin Core columns `species`, `country`, `stateProvince`, `municipality` (or `county`, where GBIF keeps the municipalities of Brazil), `locality`, `decimalLatitude`, `decimalLongitude`, `minimumElevationInMeters`, `maximumElevationInMeters`, `day`, `month`, `year`, `phenology` (or `reproductiveCondition`), `recordedBy`, `addCollector`, `recordNumber`, `collectionCode`, `catalogNumber`. Missing columns are just skipped.
- **Collectors.** The names standardized by `barroso_std()` (e.g. `D. B. O. S. Cardoso`) are written as each journal cites them. The additional collector (`addCollector`) is written as `et al.` (`& al.` in Taxon) or as the name of the second collector, e.g. `R.M. Harley & A.M. Giulietti`.
- **Phenology.** The phenology in the column `phenology` (as in records from REFLORA and JABOT) or `reproductiveCondition`, e.g. `fl`, `fl, fr`, `flower, fruit` or `st`, is written as in each journal:

  | Format | Journals |
  |---|---|
  | `(fl, fr)` | Systematic Botany, Phytotaxa, Edinburgh Journal of Botany, Acta Botanica Mexicana, Darwiniana (`(veg, fl)`), and journals whose papers show no phenology (Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society, Feddes Repertorium, PhytoKeys, Plant Ecology and Evolution, Systematics and Biodiversity, Willdenowia) |
  | `(fl., fr.)` | Taxon, Kew Bulletin, Acta Botanica Brasilica (after a comma), Botany Letters, Hoehnea, Plant Systematics and Evolution |
  | `(fl./fr.)` | Annals of the Missouri Botanical Garden |
  | `(fl. fr.)` | Nordic Journal of Botany |
  | `(fl and fr)` | Brazilian Journal of Botany |
  | `[fl, fr]` | Brittonia |
  | `fl. and fr.` | Rodriguésia, and `fl., fr.` in Candollea, without brackets |
  | `Fl., fr.` | Acta Amazonica, before the date |

  In Portuguese and Spanish, `and` becomes `e` or `y`, and sterile (`st`) becomes `est`.
- **Repeated places.** Some journals do not repeat the place of the previous specimen: `l.c.` for the same municipality in Hoehnea, and `loc. cit.` or `ídem` for the same locality in Acta Botanica Mexicana and Darwiniana.
- **Duplicates.** Duplicates of the same collection (same species, collector surname and number, or same collector, date and locality when there is no number) are written once, with all their herbaria in alphabetical order, including those found by [`barroso_flag_duplicates()`](/articles/detect_duplicates.qmd) (`duplicateCollectionCodes`).
- **Types.** The type status is not written, as types are cited apart from the examined specimens.
- **Collections without number.** The catalog number of the first herbarium is written, e.g. `R. Spruce s.n. (K000892474, LD)`, so that the specimen can be found. Use `catalog_numbers = TRUE` to write the catalog numbers of all herbaria.
- **Order.** Specimens are ordered by country, state, municipality and date. Records not identified to species are skipped.
- **Species.** For each species, a heading with the species name in italics and its author (from `scientificNameAuthorship`, `acceptedScientificName` or `scientificName`) is followed by the paragraph of its specimens.

The function returns, invisibly, a data frame with the species and their specimens, one per line, which can be checked in R:

```r
res <- barroso_write_specimens(path = "results/01Nov2026/Luetzelburgia_herbarium_records.xlsx",
                               species = "Luetzelburgia andina", verbose = FALSE)
cat(res$specimens_text)
```

## Tips

- Standardize the database first with [`barroso_std()`](/articles/standardize_specimens.qmd), so that collectors, herbarium acronyms and places are written consistently, and duplicates are removed.
- Check the countries and states of the database before writing: the specimens are cited as they are in the data.
- For the paratypes of a new species, use `species` and `header = "Paratypes"`.
